body: Replacing the legacy frozen dashboard with a modern SPA console requires a seamless single-binary distribution strategy for on-prem and local developers, while allowing containerized deployment for SaaS. This item defines the asset embedding pipeline.
_note: Full authoring of context, epic, and ACs

brief.problem: Product Forge web console and dashboard assets must be securely bundled and served directly by the platform binary without shipping exposed web source files or running Node.js at runtime.
brief.what_adds: Next-Gen Web Console Packaging Specification: embed pre-compiled SPA distribution assets into Go platform server binary.

label: PF Backlog 688
risks: Binary size increase from embedded assets mitigated via asset compression and selective asset chunking.

summary: Define and implement the build-time pipeline that embeds compiled SPA static web assets into the Go server binary via embed.FS, with support for decoupled container hosting in SaaS.
approach: Use vite build to produce static dist/, embed via go:embed in Go server binary, and catalog console asset bundle in EAP manifest.
in_scope: Go server asset embedding via embed.FS
Transparent gzip and immutable caching HTTP handlers
Web console compilation pipeline and checksum manifest
Fail-closed customer package IP protection guard
rollback: Serve web console from external static directory via configuration flag env:PF_CONSOLE_STATIC_DIR without binary rebuild.

AC-3: Shipped customer packages contain zero Node.js runtime dependencies or raw TypeScript/JSX source files.

requirements: AC-1: Web console build pipeline compiles SPA frontend into optimized HTML/JS/CSS assets with content hashing and integrity checks.
AC-2: Go platform server embeds compiled frontend assets via go:embed and serves them with HTTP cache headers and gzip compression.
AC-3: Shipped customer packages contain zero Node.js runtime dependencies or raw TypeScript/JSX source files.
invariants: SPA history fallback serves index.html for client-side routing while missing static assets return 404.
Hashed static chunks receive immutable cache headers; index.html receives no-cache headers.
Customer editions fail closed if any raw source (.ts, .tsx, .jsx, .mts, .cts), source maps (*.map), Node manifests (package.json, lockfiles), or node_modules directory is present.
SPA fallback strictly excludes /api/*, /health, and /metrics paths; unmatched API requests return 404 JSON, preserving downstream API error contracts.
Embed-time integrity attestation: NewConsoleHandler verifies embedded asset SHA256 hashes against embedded checksums.txt on startup, failing closed on tampering.

design_pack.security: Guarantees zero proprietary source code disclosure and zero Node.js runtime vulnerabilities by compiling frontend to immutable minified chunks embedded in Go binary with traversal boundary protection.
design_pack.observability: Standard HTTP access metrics, structured packaging failure codes (RAW_FRONTEND_SOURCE_DETECTED, NODE_MODULES_DETECTED, ASSET_INTEGRITY_MISMATCH), and checksum manifests.
design_pack.performance: Sub-millisecond static response times from in-memory embed.FS and 65-80% payload reduction via transparent gzip compression.
design_pack.rollout: Shipped in Go platform binary with additive EAP manifest registration.
design_pack.rollback: Serve web console from external static directory via configuration flag env:PF_CONSOLE_STATIC_DIR without binary rebuild.
decisions: DEC-1553-01: Go standard library embed.FS selected as canonical binary asset embedding mechanism.
DEC-1553-02: Hard fail-closed rejection of node_modules, source maps (*.map), and .ts/.tsx in customer packaging to protect intellectual property.

DEC-1553-03: Language rule compliance under AGENTS.md Rule 17: Extending existing shipped Python module core/packaging.py is permitted under the 60-line growth threshold, while all new shipped runtime logic and HTTP handling is authored in Go (go/web/console.go). Build-time asset compilation is tooling/packaging orchestration.
guardrails: 1. Reversibility/backup: Revert commit; optional configuration flag allows serving static assets from external directory without rebuilding binary.
2. SPOF: Go embed.FS is in-memory and stateless; static asset serving cannot crash server or block API routing.
3. Authz/RLS: Embedded assets are public web bundle; authenticated API routes handle session verification downstream.
4. Blast radius: Strictly scoped to web console static asset delivery and customer package validation; zero impact on existing API endpoints.
5. Invariants: Missing assets under /assets/ return 404; deep client links return index.html; customer packages must contain zero .ts/.jsx/node_modules.
6. Tests/rollback: Contract tests in test_web_console_packaging.py verify positive and negative failure cases. External directory serving verified.
7. API decision: needs_api=false; static asset HTTP file server and packaging validator only. No database or REST routers added.
8. Tenant isolation: N/A: embedded console assets are identical across all tenants; tenant isolation enforced at session/API layer.
9. Observability: Structured failure codes emitted during package validation with exit code 1; standard HTTP status logging.
10. Reuse: Extends existing core/packaging.py validation pipeline and standard Go net/http library.

1.response: Embed-time attestation added: NewConsoleHandler verifies embedded assets against embedded checksums.txt on startup, failing closed on tampering.

2.response: Pinned build toolchain to Node.js 20 LTS, frozen lockfile (npm ci / pnpm --frozen-lockfile), and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 in functional_spec.nfr.

3.response: Cited AGENTS.md Rule 17 in DEC-1553-03: core/packaging.py edits are under 60-line threshold; all new shipped runtime logic is in Go (go/web/console.go).

4.response: Added all 10 positive, negative, and config tests across FR-1..FR-3 in test_matrix and implementation_controls with candidate SHA.

5.response: Added X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Vary: Accept-Encoding, and Referrer-Policy to Go HTTP handler.

6.response: Established single-writer ownership in go/web: go/web/console.go is the single Go platform web console handler.

9.response: Handler checks Content-Type and skips gzip for precompressed binary assets (images, woff2, zip, gz).

10.response: Specified that PF_CONSOLE_STATIC_DIR is read once at startup with precedence over embedded assets for emergency operational rollback.

fix_impact.finding: AC-1 still unmet and prior disposition wrong: `compile_web_console` only copies + SHA256-hashes inputs — no vite/npm/pnpm compile or minify step exists anywhere in the diff, so "optimized HTML/JS/CSS" is never produced; the "ACTIONED (content-hashing)" note does not address compilation. Runtime: the AC-1 contract never executes in the pipeline.

AC-2 still unmet and prior disposition wrong: `go/web/dist` remains a hand-written placeholder (`console.log("Product Forge Web Console Initialized")`), no step wires `compile_web_console` output into `go/web/dist` (config declares `dist/console`), and no platform-server call site mounts `ServeConsoleMux`/`NewEmbeddedConsoleHandler` (separate `productforge/web` module, nothing imports it). Runtime: shipped binary serves a placeholder console; the "ACTIONED" note cites index.html rewriting, not wiring.

AC-2 pytest evidence never executes the Go handler: tests are source-greps (`assert "..." in src_text`) plus `test_console_behavioral_simulation_http`, which runs a Python `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` re-implementation. Runtime: any Go regression (headers, gzip, routing, traversal) ships with a green pipeline while `go test` may not run in CI.

`compile_web_console` still never cleans `output_dist_dir` (prior disposition claims it does): stale hashed assets from earlier builds persist, get embedded, and `VerifyAssetIntegrity`'s unlisted-asset fail-closed rule trips. Runtime: server refuses to boot after any rebuild that leaves a leftover file.

Hash renaming still rewrites only `index.html`; `url(...)`/dynamic-import references inside CSS/JS keep pre-rename filenames. Prior disposition cited `isContentHashedAsset` (caching), not rewriting — disposition wrong. Runtime: real SPA bundle 404s its own fonts/chunks on first load.

`test_console_embedded_distribution_assets_exist` normalizes CRLF before hashing (`replace(b"\r\n", b"\n")`), masking line-ending drift. Runtime: test passes on a CRLF checkout while Go's integrity check hash-mismatches and the server fails closed at startup.
